headline_marked: [[Sugon reveals 'world's first' 64-thread mobile workstation for AI]] with domestic CPU, 16GB VRAM
headline: Sugon reveals 'world's first' 64-thread mobile workstation for AI with domestic CPU, 16GB VRAM
summary: This next-gen device promises cloud-level AI performance, delivering up to 50 tokens/second on local 35B MoE models, all within a surprisingly thin 0.665-inch form factor.
details: Chinese supercomputer manufacturer Sugon has teased an upcoming mobile workstation designed for AI performance. It features a domestic 64-thread processor and 16GB of VRAM, capable of delivering up to 50 tokens per second on local 35-billion-parameter Mixture of Experts (MoE) AI models.

Unlike bulkier portable workstations, Sugon's device maintains a traditional laptop form factor. Measuring just 0.665 inches (16.9 mm) thick, it aligns with the thin and lightweight premium laptop category, only slightly thicker than many ultrabooks.

Sugon does not produce its own processors but is the largest shareholder in Hygon, a company with a history of leveraging licensed Zen IP from AMD. It is highly probable that Hygon will supply the CPU for this new mobile workstation.

While the exact processor model is unconfirmed, Hygon has offered 32-core, 64-thread chips for years. The mobile workstation might utilize Hygon's latest C86-5G chips, which claim a "new self-developed microarchitecture" and support four-way simultaneous multithreading (SMT4).

If equipped with a C86-5G chip, it would likely be a 16-core, 64-thread configuration, providing substantial processing power for AI. The inclusion of 16GB of VRAM confirms a discrete graphics card, which Sugon claims will offer 3X to 5X faster AI inference than mainstream products.

The stated performance of 50 tokens per second on a 35B MoE model is comparable to standard cloud APIs, which typically range from 30 to 80 tokens per second. This suggests the mobile workstation could be a significant advancement for local AI workloads.

Sugon has not yet disclosed official availability or pricing for the mobile workstation. Given the current market for high-performance memory and storage, the device is anticipated to carry a premium price tag.

headline_marked: Samsung Z Fold 8 [[outsells Ultra brother]] in South Korea, becomes best-selling foldable
headline: Samsung Z Fold 8 outsells Ultra brother in South Korea, becomes best-selling foldable
summary: The Galaxy Z Fold 8's wider aspect ratio and practical design have led to unexpected success, even cannibalizing production lines for future smartphones to meet demand.
details: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 has achieved remarkable success, reportedly outselling its Ultra counterpart in South Korea and becoming Samsung's best-selling foldable device to date. This unexpected triumph highlights a shift in consumer preference towards practical and innovative foldable designs.

Despite its $1,900 price tag, the Z Fold 8 sold out on Amazon shortly after its launch, with other retailers struggling to keep up with demand. Samsung has even resorted to reallocating production from future Galaxy smartphones to meet the current demand for the Z Fold 8.

The key to the Z Fold 8's success lies in its wider aspect ratio, a design previously seen on devices like the Huawei Pura X and Oppo Find N2. This form factor, while not entirely new, offers practical benefits for foldable phone usage, proving that innovation doesn't always require a completely novel design.

Reviewers have praised the Z Fold 8, with one stating it's the 'big surprise of 2026' and the phone they've 'enjoyed discovering the most.' The device is seen as a significant win for Samsung and a positive development for the broader Android market, demonstrating the potential for practical design choices to drive sales.

The success of the Z Fold 8 could inspire other manufacturers to explore more practical and impactful design changes in the smartphone industry. In an era where flagship phones often look indistinguishable, the Z Fold 8's success underscores the value of unique yet functional design elements.
